feedback: This candidate changes one thing from the baseline: kd goes from 0.05 to 0.30. The baseline evidence (iteration 0, 60 trials across oval, s-bend and slalom) supports the change. Every run went off track, with max_error about 0.060 to 0.061 m, against an off-track limit of 0.06 m. Each run also had exactly one line-loss event, and progress was only 0.035 to 0.115. Steering oscillation was low (0.064 to 0.074), so the baseline was not jittering. It was slow to correct on bends, which points to missing derivative damping. kd = 0.05 times the rate of change of the signal is close to nothing, so this is a sound test. kp, ki, base_speed, sensor layout, weights and line_loss are all unchanged, so the race isolates the effect of kd. I checked the geometry and sign conventions: sensor weights run -1 to +1 from right to left, and the signal and wheel equations are consistent. The candidate is valid and is a clear improvement in exploration value over the baseline, so I approve it to race. Read the telemetry for the next step. (a) If max_error falls below 0.06 and line_loss_events drops, keep kd and test base_speed 1.8 to see whether speed can rise while the robot stays on the line. (b) If the robot still leaves the track with line_loss_events still at 1, test line_loss = search_right or search_left, since last_direction did not recover the line on any baseline track. (c) If steering_oscillation rises well above 0.15, kd is too aggressive for the 10 ms loop. Then try kd about 0.15 before lowering kp. If the robot completes but completion_time is above 2.5 s, raise base_speed in steps of about 0.2. Change one field group at a time so each effect stays attributable.
requested_changes: If the robot still goes off track with line_loss_events at 1, change line_loss from last_direction to search_right or search_left. Baseline: last_direction gave exactly one line-loss event per run on all three tracks.

If max_error falls below 0.06 but progress or completion stays low, raise base_speed from 1.6 to about 1.8 with kd at 0.30. Baseline: progress was only 0.04 to 0.12, so pace is a possible limit once the line is held.

If steering_oscillation rises well above the baseline 0.06 to 0.07 (for example above 0.15), reduce kd to about 0.15 and keep kp at 4.0. Baseline: kd was 0.05, so 0.30 is a six-fold change and could over-damp or add jitter.
